big_case.notes: Significant Solicitor General emergency application resulting in a 6-page published per curiam opinion clarifying that major-questions challenges to agency action remain statutory rather than constitutional claims under Dalton v. Specter for purposes of IIRIRA § 102(c)(2)(A)'s jurisdiction strip, and unblocking over 300 miles of southern-border barrier construction.

leakage.notes: Forward prediction run on 2026-10-23 while the event was open. The predictor used CourtListener RECAP tools to read the underlying W.D. Tex. docket (No. 3:26-cv-01099-KC, docket ID 72652572) filings dated between 2026-08-11 and 2026-10-21 (including the Oct. 14 preliminary-injunction opinion and Oct. 21 stay denial), all of which preceded the Supreme Court event cutoff.

central_claims.basis: The November 9, 2026 per curiam opinion granted an unqualified stay pending the filing and disposition of a petition for a writ of certiorari (pp. 5-6) without granting certiorari or summarily reversing.
central_claims.claim: The Court will grant the application in full for a stay pending the filing and disposition of a petition for a writ of certiorari and decline to grant certiorari before judgment or summarily reverse.

central_claims.basis: The per curiam opinion held that the district court likely lacked jurisdiction under § 102(c)(2)(A), citing Dalton, 511 U.S. at 472-473, and Clark, 543 U.S. at 381, to explain that invoking a canon of statutory construction grounded in constitutional separation-of-powers principles does not convert a statutory claim into a constitutional one (pp. 3-5).
central_claims.claim: The Court will hold that the district court likely lacked jurisdiction under IIRIRA § 102(c)(2)(A) because, under Dalton v. Specter, 511 U.S. 462 (1994), and Clark v. Martinez, 543 U.S. 371 (2005), a major-questions argument is a statutory-interpretation claim rather than a constitutional claim.

central_claims.basis: The per curiam opinion included an '[i]n any event' merits holding that the Secretary had clear congressional authorization under § 102(a) and (c)(1) and that nothing in IIRIRA required a comparative approach to 'high illegal entry' (p. 5).
central_claims.claim: Even if reached on the merits, the waivers fall within the Secretary's express statutory discretion under IIRIRA § 102(a) and (c)(1), and 'areas of high illegal entry' does not require a comparative sector-by-sector test (citing In re Border Infrastructure Environmental Litigation).

central_claims.basis: Because the per curiam opinion resolved likelihood of success on the threshold jurisdictional bar and statutory authorization, it did not address remedial overbreadth or cite Trump v. CASA.
central_claims.claim: The Court will also fault the preliminary injunction as overbroad under Trump v. CASA, Inc., 606 U.S. 831 (2025), for enjoining barrier construction across 300+ miles beyond the parcels tied to plaintiffs' demonstrated standing.

central_claims.basis: Only Justice Jackson noted that she would deny the application for stay (p. 6).
central_claims.claim: Justices Sotomayor, Kagan, and Jackson will note dissents from the stay grant.
